opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: covers the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government; ordinarily resident in Scotland with at least two years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, or a substantial and recent connection to Scotland; entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK or hold Limited Leave to Remain/asylum seeker; enrolled on an eligible undergraduate degree course at a Scottish HEI (or a course validated by one of these universities); not already graduated with a degree (except under the second-degree reskilling scheme).
opportunities.summary: Grants covering tuition fees for undergraduate study at Scottish higher education institutions for students from low-income households who are not eligible for government tuition fee funding. Open for applications from 1 June 2026 to 5pm 1 December 2026 for academic year 2026-27.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants, plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to those undertaking the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh (awarded by University of Edinburgh); must satisfy course entry criteria and be accepted onto the MSc (full-time or part-time); reside in a low-income household; be ordinarily resident in Scotland; demonstrate at least two years of Scottish secondary schooling/college education or a substantive connection to Scotland; be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK; have drawn down SAAS living-cost loan or be able to cover living costs; not eligible for public grant funding; not already hold a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: A partnership between Carnegie Education Fund and the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh providing funding for Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households to undertake the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (SCQF Level 11) in plant science and botany, covering full tuition fees and a living-cost bursary.
